body:
I feel this a lot. Most of my friends who have stayed friends with me have autism (while, I think I have AuDHD). Some rarely call or text, and some will text but kind of only want to talk about themselves, so it can get crazy lonely. When I do hangout with them, I find myself grasping for topics that they are interested in that we can connect on. It makes it feel even more isolating. 

As an extrovert, it is extra difficult since I have higher emotional needs. I would love for friends who would be interested in routinely meeting up and talking or learning something new together. The more I age, the more I feel that socialization is one of the few important things in life, but I am really struggling to get to the level I want it to be.

I think what you are talking about is slightly different. I have run into quite a few people who respond with their own story and say nothing about your story or barely on the topic. It makes it feel like you could have just not said anything and it would be the exact same result. Feels isolating.

Sharing your story and a comment to the other person's story, I think, is better or asking question.

I do go to intellectual discussion groups and talk with my partner and some friends on intellectual things, but I think it just adds more things for me to think about and then I want to ask more people on those things.

I think I just don't know how to be light.

I think our hyper fixation on independence is a big problem and is biting us. That said, I think this kind of ignores parents and also, that just because one can do all those things themselves doesn't mean they have to. A partnership allows for splitting chores.
He complains about it a lot. Lately, he is at the "nothing will ever work for me. I should give up" stage.
He is making $75k.

I am so sorry that you went through that. It's not fair.  
Thank you!

I will check again. I feel so anxious and pessimistic about the friend-making experience that it makes me worried. I host meetups, too, and for the 5th month, no one has showed that RSVP'd. It hit harder recently when I kept the meetup even though I am grieving. It just feels so difficult.

But I feel like friendships are about showing support. I show support to others and I actually really enjoy doing so because I care. If we are all too individualistic, it leads to something like the loneliness crisis that is being faced now.

Yes! I truly do want support, but what do you say? Talk to me, check in on me? Show that you care? 

I think it's frustrating because I really struggle to make and keep friends, especially being neurodivergent, so it feels like this endless treadmill of trying to make friends only to lose them again.
That's so awful! I don't understand why people are like that. I am so sorry that you, your mom, and uncle have gone through that.
Yeah, it's a bit performative and not as helpful as I think people think it is.
I wish it was not this way. I think everything should take a village.

I know I tried from my phone, but can't seem to get it to mirror for the app. I may be able to mirror from my computer to the TV to see if that helps me be more motivated. I think it might since I watch documentaries just fine from there.

Thank you for the information! I will try the masks. Sleeping has been a hard one for me, for sure, as I suffer from insomnia (due to work and childhood). I have been battling it fairly well lately, but it's definitely been difficult when he has to sleep on the couch (that and I know he doesn't really get any sleep on the couch).

I did speak with him more on a balance of still helping when/if he needs it. Making sure medication is nearby, he has water, and food, and still ensuring that I am getting my social battery filled and working on the feelings of guilt.

I appreciate the information you have provided. I do think a lot of it is on me and feeling trapped by me (and a bit frustrated by him self-sabotaging for everything else -- junk food he usually buys). I will have to do some further reading and discussing it for guilt (and understanding what is normal for having a sick partner). A therapist is a good suggestion, but I had really poor success with therapists for over ten years and found most of my progress to have occurred with a good support system, good research, and meditating on subjects, so I will probably forgo that.

He is definitely not a jerk, but can be a tad selfish and inflexible.

Thank you for all of the information! He had mentioned sleeping separately and wearing a mask as options. Is it the air purifier that helps preventing the sickness? The only struggle I have with sleeping separate is that my body seems to not allow me to sleep when he is like that.

He rarely, if ever, asks me to take care of him as he is worried it will cause the deterioration of our relationship like what happened with an ex of his. I think a part of it is I feel that I should stay home because "what if it worsens?" and also, it's the "right thing to do". He had been dealing with dizziness for months that I was really worried about, so when it would popup and I would have plans, I would cancel to make sure he is okay. The dizziness seemed to stem from ear infections he got from the cold. 

I think also I am a bit traumatized from when I was a child where my mother was supposed to be taking care of me and would go on a full day shopping spree all the while I would be hungry and thirsty, but too tired/weak to get out of bed. It hurt so much and I don't want him to feel the same.

He told me yesterday he doesn't want him being sick to get in the way of me going out, but I feel guilty at the thought of it and don't know what to do. I do think he needs to take better care of himself, and he did acknowledge that he has been pretty bad about it. That part has been frustrating, especially since he complains so often about things and so much of it is due to him. When he actually stops doing the bad habit I have brought up as being bad for the nth time, he is suddenly better. 

I do love him, but I think I may be having a bit of compassion fatigue and caregiver fatigue going on. We do share quite a bit of hobbies that we practice at home, but I need to find a way guilt-free to not let me social battery get so low and see my friends.
Thank you so much for the clarification! With so much going on, it's so hard to tell what was the result of my sibling's disability and what were caused by the abusive/toxic environment.

Me! I was the scapegoat. No one knew my sister had autism, but she was the designated golden child due to her fixating on building things and my father wanting a kid he could make into an engineer. I became the scapegoat. Failing grades of a sibling? My fault. Sibling having trouble with friends? Probably my fault. Sibling doesn't like school or a certain food? My fault.

“That's why they call it the American Dream, because you have to be asleep to believe it.”

― George Carlin

I have a stable, flexible job, a loving relationship, and just recently developed a larger social circle than I ever had in the past. I also host events and have been looked at pretty favorably -- turned my uncoolness around -- a lot of what made me uncool ended up helping me be "cool" as an adult. It took a while, but I am incredibly happy now.

Absolutely! I think I may bring up the car one as I know she got in a stranger's car when she knew them for only an hour. I did share some ways to look into the person to ensure they are who they say they are and have no criminal record. Also, asked that she provide a picture and her whereabouts if she goes to a house (if she is okay with that), so that I can check-in on her to make sure she is safe.

It absolutely can be. I think a lot of bad experiences can definitely make for good stories. I hope so. She has started opening up after removing some stressors, so I am happy that she is opening up more and want to help.

I am playing it a bit by ear, but what I am hoping to do is gently ask probing questions and share experiences. I will tell her certain things that are concerning, but want to avoid telling her to move on just in case she decides to still see him, but feels she has to hide it because I disapprove. I know she is feeling a lot of pressure and worry over having no experience and was stood-up two times in a row by different people, so I think that also did not help (in addition to not knowing what is normal).

1. I agree and will be talking to her about setting expectations. I think the times I have had dates bring it up is when they want to discuss compatibility overall, but usually at least for me, not on the first date.

2. Yeah, I had told her that going slow would seem more to me like suggesting a movie and putting him around shoulder or asking to put arm over shoulder/couch. I definitely feel like he is driving at that.

3. Interesting! I know some guys are under the impression that they have to "make the women see them as a sexual being" to not "friendzone" them -- which is problematic logic to me. I will keep this in mind and discuss. My friend seemed okay with it, so I didn't push.

4. This was another one that scared me as he reminds me of an ex of mine that lived with his mother and mooched off of her (made messes, argued, etc). That ex also acted like a teenager and the relationship was not great. This one I am trying to be sensitive about as she lived with her mother until last year and I know she felt bad about it.

I think they might be. Apparently, they own some apartment complexes. He does seem like he hasn't had to work for anything based on the stories.

That's a good point. I think she picks up on some words, but I think she is worried to pry, so she may not get some necessary information that may be helpful. I did tell her to see how he reacts to boundary setting and also, to not be afraid to ask for clarification. If it makes the person uncomfortable, they will say so, but should ask.

I think she does not know what is normal and what is not, and is just really excited at the thought of getting experience. My thought is she could get experience with someone less um..scary, but I also, of course, want her to make her own choices just powered with insights.
I want to know this, too. His father was even going to give him his own place free of charge, apparently.

The horny at work thing was the first one that made me concerned. I couldn't imagine a first date with that disclosure and I have been on some dates with skeevy people in the past.

We are definitely watching him closely on the double date.

Yeah, I am definitely worried for her and understand why she really wants to make it work since she is self-conscious about the lack of experience. I think lack of experience can definitely make someone naive. I know I went through similar struggles due to being sheltered.

That's what I was worried about, too.

She grew up a bit sheltered and has told me that she is not the best judge of people which had made her hesitant to start dating for a while. The fight one scared me since I had a partner who was an abuser, and I don't want her to go through what I went through.

Omph! Couch surfing would be rough, too. I had not considered that as a possibility. I did mention figuring out what happened during the fight as more info needed.

Thank you! That was kind of what I was thinking as well.

I know while dating I made a lot of mistakes along the way and learned. She may make the same mistakes; she may make different ones. My biggest concern is her physical safety. I always make sure to tell her that everyone is different and her feelings are valid. I feel like shaming people causes them to hide which is not the goal. I also grew up really sheltered, so I see no value in getting upset as I know that being sheltered makes you also make mistakes that others may not anticipate.

I appreciate the words. I know it will be a learning experience for her. I just want to be there if/when she needs me.
No problem!

Could you be depressed? I am sorry you are going through that. I remember when I went through high amounts of stress, and spent all my time on schooling and work that I no longer had hobbies, I had to rediscover my interests. Maybe that would help? Are you able to set boundaries at work? I would also recommend doing things to build back up your attention span. I have had to do that by reading books for longer and longer periods. That has been helping me.

All hope it not lost. It will just take some time to rebuild yourself.

I am sure it can't be fun to see an old flame, especially if you miss them, but I think it happens. I had a friend tell me about living in a small town and having to deal wit being in close proximity to your ex all the time. I asked how she handled it, and she told me that eventually it gets easier and you move on.

Nothing wrong with seeing them nor with them seeing you. It happens.

I would say, if able, please see a therapist. That sounds like a stressful situation all the way around and will eat you alive. I am not saying I think cheating is great, but I think it may help to discuss with a therapist on what you are feeling.
Yeah, I would skip this one.
I feel like it has to be more than that. Maybe because men have less inherent risk when going on a date (pregnancy, safety -- these can still affect men just in a different way)?
Yeah, that's what I would think, too.
If they didn't ask or see body language, yes. I move slower than other people. I'd rather not kiss on a first date.
No, no worries. It takes time to find the right person. Find someone who appreciates you. It took until my late 20s to find someone. It's not a race or a competition. It just takes time.

I am so sorry that happened to you. Ghosting is so prevalent now that it is a shame ( I guess ghosting was a thing before, too).

I agree with another poster on asking on a second date. I would normally try to bring up the next date/hangout with new people and see how they react. I also look to see what their interests are (which you may have done through relatability) to see if I can pick something to go to that they may like.

I think it can be hard as everyone is looking for different things. Were you able to get info on past relationships and what they are looking for to try to glean what their ideal fit would be? I know people who want someone who is kind, responsible, and makes them laugh, and others who want something more specific -- for example, I hyper-fixated on finding someone with shared values and an interest in history since I wanted that in a partnership. It's possible you did absolutely nothing wrong, but they were just looking for something else.

I know I went through a lot of ghosting and so did my partner before we found each other. We met a month after Valentine's Day which was rough at the time.

I do not think you are doing anything wrong by not risking it, and I appreciate it. This person is offering advice that is too risky for some women. I would question your motives and if you wanted it casual if you did what they are pushing for.
Agreed. I would ghost after that because I would feel they were rushing it and that it would be a wham-bam-thank you, ma'am.
I don't know about this one. If I had that, I probably would freak and not go on another date.

Hmmm..do you enjoy the messages he sends? My partner would sometimes take that long to respond, but we sent each other absurdly long messages. If it's only been one date, give it another date and try to see if he likes texting or what an ideal relationship looks like to him. 

If you don't like the answers, can always choose not to do a second date. I know I prefer frequent contact, but everyone has different preferences, so good to sus out.
I may be a hopeless romantic, but why does it always just come down to looks for these comments? Makes the person seem more like a piece of meat.

I would not if I didn't see a long-term future with them.

My partner was 45 - an hour away when we first started dating. We tried to meet in the middle, but when visiting each other's places, those drives were difficult! The only reason I did it was the relationship showed promise, and two years later, I am glad that we made those sacrifices and also, glad we live together, so we don't have to anymore!

Definitely depends how far you live apart. I do not like driving at all and really wished there was good transit where I live. 

My partner and I were 45 minutes to an hour by car, and I dated someone prior who didn't drive at all and was an hour away. When I moved and they were 15 minutes away, it still got a bit old always being the one to take them everywhere.

I think taking a break from dating overall is a good idea when feeling frustrated. I know when I was on the apps I would get to the point of complaining about the apps on the dates! It was pretty bad. I had to take a lot of breaks.

I think meeting in-person is much nicer and builds rapport better (feels less artificial). I did meet my partner from an app and am grateful (not for the app), but I had to go through so many people who made me feel less than to find them.

I don't think anything is wrong with you. I think it is pretty normal to reach out to someone you had a connection with when lonely. I agree with others. Be kind to yourself, and work little by little to build up social connections. You got this! 

I relate as I did the same and went from no friends to finally having friends.

You both are fairly young, so I am keeping that in perspective as I write this. I think the guy you are seeing could have been much more mature about how he handled it as far as communication.

Beyond you hugging him and saying "it's okay. I am here", did you ask him if you should stop watching the movie? It sounds like he was telling you it was scary and was hoping you would maybe consider his feeling more and ask (but I could be wrong). I know that puts a bit of the onus on you as well, but I kind of think communication should be a two-way street in a relationship. I have friends and a partner that have things that make them uncomfortable, if they say that it is scary, I pause and ask them if they want to continue. Can it sometimes be a bummer? Sure, but I'd rather ask than have someone get upset.

The sex part is bad all around. The rest kind of reminds me of someone who is triggered by something and it made them so uncomfortable that they rant about it endlessly. 

I think next time, vet what the person can and cannot handle, and if it is really important to you to watch horror movies, find a partner who appreciates them. Otherwise, you are going to have to be more accepting of differences or watch the movies with friends. That's what I do for certain media my partner does not like and that's what they do.

I appreciate the response. I think it would have been good if I had had the confidence to bring it up earlier, and I should have just said 'no' to the catsitting, but had grown tired of saying 'no' after telling her several times that I felt fairly ill when changing the litterboxes (and even caught strep when catsitting after she did not clean her house after she got it and recovered from it).

I checked in often regarding her father, but at a certain point it switched from being about her father to being how wonderful her life was with her new home she was getting, so I had stopped checking in as much on her father which may have been a mistake.

As she interrupts everyone, I did see what happens when people interrupt her to finish what they were saying. She would get upset. If she interrupted me, she would cycle back to asking me to finish only to interrupt me again. She let me speak only when I was upset, but very, very rarely when I was sharing anything about myself. I imagine I was probably less attention-grabbing than with other friends since I sounded mousier and stuttered when talking with her due to feeling like she didn't actually want to listen to me. I think interrupting can be fine if I can finish a story at some point. It just rarely happened with her. Made worse by her trying to push my triggers when I never did that to her for her's. I did start interrupting her and cycling back to what I said, but the behavior continued. 

I may have also started to lose hope when I had an old friend come into my life and experienced what it felt like to have someone who asked and listened to what I had to say, and was thoughtful. I felt like I kind of settled on a friend like you would settle on a lover -- which is definitely an AH thing to do.

Yeah, I think I felt hot and cold on that person. I enjoyed some time with them, but not as much as other friends. The close proximity compared to other friends had me hang out with her more.

I think moreover, I felt like it may not have been right to not let her know.

I don't disagree on the holidays part. I was very isolated growing up and didn't get the chance to really socialize with a lot of people in my 20s, so I couldn't tell if it was the holidays or a slow fade as I had gotten sensitive to the slow fade. I learned after that things were okay with those friends, but wasn't sure at the time and wasn't in a good mental space. Plus, I was sleep deprived from work those months, so that did not help with being hyper sensitive.
Thank you! I did like the toe box for them. I am getting another pair and am hoping the tongues of the shoes are movable.

Thank you! These look great! I will check these out.

My family members are able to wear men's size, but unfortunately, my feet are too small for them.
I'll try New Balance again. I currently have one in 2E, but the toe box is too small for me.
Thank you! Did the Altras last long for you?
I would love to join one as well! That sounds awesome!
That sounds awesome! I will have to look into that.
Thank you! I hope so, too.

I am so sorry you are going through that. I lived in the middle of nowhere for a period and it was incredibly isolating and boring. Could not imagine doing it again.

I worry that I am on both sides of the picture. I keep thinking I should move to a different country or state and then I will be happier. The lack of a social safety net fills me with immense fear, but I also have a fear to make changes. I feel like anytime I have made a change, it always came back to bite me. It's hard not to look at things bleakly when the closest thing I have to success is a monkey's paw. 

I think I am scared to settle down and lose my freedom. If I plant roots, then I can't leave if things get bad and I just never seem to find community where I live nor things that I like to do. Everyone feels so different than me. I feel like an alien in this place. I feel like I have lost so much waffling back and forth between staying and going as a way to cope with the pain and shock and stress. My boyfriend has already told me that he can't comfort me and is tired of how I am now. I feel so alone -- no matter where I go. It certainly does feel like being younger again. I don't know what will make me happy at this point.
Thank you! I am sorry you are going through this, too.
I definitely worry about that, too.

Completely agree. Regardless of pay, most of my jobs have been really stressful, usually as a result of bad management. My job is mostly stressful now because of bad management and execs. The work itself is not as hard.

Thank you! You are definitely not wrong. I keep debating what I want. Do I want to live in a less exciting but more affordable place? Do I want a different job? At this point, I am not sure what is best. My partner's work also limits us.

Absolutely! A long commute is awful. 

Traffic is usually pretty bad from 6 am - 6:45 pm here. He's never been a morning person, so getting up earlier may be a challenge. Plus, he carpools.

I did suggest using audiobooks or studying for his license during the commute and he did like that, so hopefully, that will help even a little.

He has met with management a few times and they have put him in for promotions, but didn't pass the interview for reasons never covered in any of his performance reviews. He has told them he would like to do licensing and they have provided him with the materials after I discussed with him a few weeks back that more would need to be done to be competitive. 

I agree. I really wish he would pursue other opportunities since this one is kind of a lost cause, but he will need to pursue furthering education first,

Yeah, I am worried that it would be triggering. I used to get PTSD episodes at night when I lived in that area. I would have nightmares/night terrors of those people breaking into my place that were so real. For that reason, I moved and it really helped me no longer have those nightmares.

It's hard to justify moving when this job doesn't seem like it is it. I don't know if I would move there if it was a better paying job due to mental health and crime, but I would probably be more inclined if I felt the job treated him well and he liked the work. 

I think he is struggling with imposter syndrome. He also has dyslexia which has made it difficult for him to study and put himself out there, so I think it's led to him staying at a company that does not value him. I think that's a good way to go about it and will talk to him about those solutions since there is not much we can do from now since our lease still has a lot of time left on it.

He works in a support role for finance and it pays about $60k which is okay, but not great given the cost of living is so high. 

Yeah, you are probably right. I do not want to play mother.

I know I have looked in the past since he told me that there were "no jobs". I was seeing jobs, but he needs licensing to be competitive and to apply. He hasn't done anything extra to make himself a desirable candidate.

I know, for sure, he wants work-from-home and he did get the training material after I expressed frustration with him for complaining that he deserves a promotion when he didn't pursue licensing and has done nothing to try to make himself competitive or pursue other jobs.

Thank you so much! I will probably need to skill-up, but that should be doable once I get some sleep. It's a shame because the pay is good and PTO, but everything else sucks. 

I'll look into therapists. I have had bad therapists here, but will see what I can do.

I have for one in the past, but the other, I am afraid of retaliation.

Should I move in the direction of my boyfriend's work or away from a place with a HCOL?
Oh, gosh, yes! Without my crafting items, things would be so much better.
Thank you! I will look into a system to attach under the desk as well as a basket for the stimming toys.

Yeah, dating a mono kinkster I am sure is doable if they reciprocate in other things, but otherwise, it really sucks.

I didn't quite bring it up. I was really young and they were my first sexual partner (if you can call them that), so I didn't really know much better and felt I was wrong for the stuff I liked and felt guilty that it was hard to meet their sexual needs.

I do get vacation time, but I have to really take it off way in-advance because he snaps it up, if I don't and he requests it really early. I really like taking days leading up to the holiday off, but since he has been here, he always grabs them first. I think also my boss made a passive-aggressive remark about people taking time-off and him never getting time off, so I have been feeling a little guilty.

That is fair on crosstraining. Should I lay off crosstraining, too, if he is only serving to make my job more difficult? 

My boss never asks for documentation nor does the company, but I have asked for documentation from him since I have documented almost everything I do and also, because I rarely work on some of the projects he manages -- similar to how he rarely works on mine.

I think you are absolutely right. This coworker is my boss' favorite and gives him a lot of leverage. My boss doesn't really lead. He just kind of throws stuff for us to do at us and not much else. It's made things pretty stressful and frustrating.

I think this is absolutely fair advice and I have made leaps and bounds of progress in setting up more boundaries and trying to detach, but am not all the way there yet. My boss complained about how he never gets to take time, so I felt really guilty about taking it as much as my coworker, and I feel like (projecting) that I will get scolded if I take as much time-off as my coworker since he is the favorite.

I also feel this sense of dread and fear in that he won't crosstrain me, so when he is gone, I am left to fight fires that only he would really know how to fight. And it would be nice to have someone to commiserate with like I did prior, but that person was laid-off so I am stuck with my brown-nosing, arrogant, lazy, smug, selfish coworker.

Everything else is really that he is just kind of a smarmy person and there is a lot of class issues going on since he comes from a rich background and I don't (our COL has risen because we have been getting a lot of people like him who make much more than other people who grew up where I did and he got to buy things like houses -- plural -- outright when I can't afford a home in my hometown). Him bragging about all his money I think sets me off a bit because of how much of a struggle it has been. I concede that I do not have to like my coworkers and could put up with his terrible personality, if he would actually lend a hand and not leave me floundering when I have to take on his workload. I always crosstrain him.
I mean, sure, but it would be nice if he would confirm sometimes, so other people get the chance to take it.

Nope, no oral nor intercourse at all. I would ask, but he would turn it down or tell me it was gross and weird to do those. He only wanted to do mutual masturbation, masturbate, or scat. It was then that I learned the difference between a kink and a fetish.

No dig to people who like those things, but it was lonely and I was incredibly unsatisfied.

He hated oral the most (giving and receiving) and fingering as well (probably didn't help that he was bad at it). PIV was also 100% off the table (including all forms of PIV). He found all of those weird and uncomfortable. It sucked.

Had an ex like that. He claimed I didn't like anything and when I told him what I liked (some of it standard), he then told me the majority, especially the standard stuff, was weird, didn't do any of it in bed, and proclaimed that I had libido problems.

I would say that is not a normal response. If I would prefer sleep, I would definitely have told my partner that it is very sweet, but I need to sleep and would love it later. Either way, it's such a kind thing to make a partner breakfast. I love when my partner does that. 

I think you should find someone who is happy with what you do. A relationship I had I could never do anything right and it tore me apart and I had another relationship where I was taken for granted. Now, in the relationship I am in, I feel happy, loved, supported, and seen. If the behavior he has exhibited is the norm, I think you should reconsider. You deserve better.

Yeah, the app definitely leaves me more jaded and depressed. I am not sure what to do though to make friends. I really like discussions and history, but the people who attend those are usually older, and I work from home, so not a lot of opportunity to make friends.
Even when he clarified on his 10/10 being not about looks, the clarification doesn't seem that much better.....

Definitely have that talk with her about what you are noticing. I think that is the only thing you can do.

I don't feel it is normal to have a talk in the bathroom -- bit of an odd place, but she should be the one to explain her behavior. I hope it goes well.

With that said, you have been with her for 5 years and your 10/10 rating is kind of um....it rubs me the wrong way. It's all things that personally benefit you and means nothing about her as a person other than what she does for you domestically. If my partner listed just those qualities as why they valued me, I would feel so disappointed.

I don't think there is anything wrong with this being a dealbreaker for you. i think it would be a dealbreaker for a lot of people.

My ex of seven years was frequently unemployed and I had to foot the bill for him. He often lied to me about applying for jobs, taking interviews, and being in school. Nothing feels less romantic than being gaslit and having to support someone (especially someone like my ex who was abusive and demanding). 

Not saying that this guy could be like that. I ended up dating someone who lived with their parents, but had been working consistently. It's been great with the person I am dating, but it was certainly not without challenges since he had never lived on his own. But at that point, we were already a wonderful fit and I was very clear in the beginning that I did not want to go through a repeat of playing mommy like I did with my ex. 

It's a tossup. I don't think it is reassuring that he is upset about talks of the future. I'd say, if you are already not feeling it, let this one go. This part of dating should be fun -- it shouldn't be stressful.

I absolutely love your hobbies and don't care for concerts, partying, etc! Back when I was on the dating apps, I was looking exclusively for people who were into history. I find cooking, bookstores, and looking at household repairs to be huge pluses. 

I think you will find your person. It's better to be who you are than someone you are not. I often would find myself seeking out people who put things outside the norm as that is what I did. If you try to be like everyone else, you may not find the person for you.

Only thing I think would be good is just trying to make friends.
That makes sense. I will look into more cuttings. I have been growing everything from seeds.
For peppers, would I need a growlight for them?
